intended_missing_claim: No one-suture disk for a diagrammatically prime reduced alternating checkerboard.

hypotheses: N has a finite proper disk system Δ; cutting N along all its disks gives balls.
The suture s meets ∂Δ transversely, and on each cut ball the suture arcs form a graph whose vertices are the disk spots.
Each such graph is connected, loop-free, bridge-free, and has no cut vertex; there are at least two vertices.
proof_outline: Choose a one-suture disk X minimizing |∂X∩∂Δ|. Remove circle components of X∩Δ by innermost Δ-disk surgery, retaining the disk component with original boundary.

If X∩Δ has arcs, its dual tree has at least two leaves. At most one outermost subdisk contains the sole suture intersection; choose another with boundary arc α on the punctured boundary sphere disjoint from s.
Both ends of α lie on one disk spot v. Join them across v to form a Jordan circle. If other disk spots lie on both sides, deleting v disconnects the suture graph, contradiction.
Thus one side contains no other spots. Because the graph is loop-free and α misses it, that side contains no suture edges. Hence α is boundary-parallel across a disk disjoint from s.
If other portions of ∂X lie in that boundary disk, choose an innermost one; a boundary isotopy disjoint from s removes two intersections with ∂Δ, contradicting minimality.

If X∩Δ is empty, its boundary lies on one ball boundary sphere and crosses the suture graph once. Spots on both sides make that crossed edge a bridge; spots on just one side force an even intersection count. Either is impossible.

checkerboard_realization_to_verify.spine: The checkerboard retracts to its planar Tait graph G. A round regular neighborhood of that planar spine can serve as a thickening of the surface, independently of the signed half-twists.
checkerboard_realization_to_verify.disks: Complementary face disks of G cut the complementary handlebody into the two upper/lower balls.
checkerboard_realization_to_verify.suture_tracing: Alternation (uniform signed half-twists) should arrange exactly one suture crossing on each diagram-edge segment of each dual disk boundary. The upper overpass and lower underpass at a crossing then give the edge of the opposite Tait graph. This local chart must be verified explicitly; not yet used as a proved premise.
checkerboard_realization_to_verify.graph_properties: Reducedness gives dual loop/bridge absence. Diagrammatic primeness gives absence of cut vertices via the boundary of a planar regular neighborhood of an incident graph block. These planar implications need complete local writing.
